newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF team ends Russian monitoring visit.
newsitem.headline: IMF team ends Russian monitoring visit.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund mission has completed a regular monthly review of the Russian economy and is due to leave on Friday, chief representataive Thomas Wolf said.
However, a decision on paying the next tranche of a $10 billion, three-year IMF loan may not be taken until early next month, after the IMF/World Bank annual meetings in Washington.

The IMF delayed a tranche of some $330 million in the summer because of concern about lower than forecast tax revenues but handed over the money last month. it paid a further tranche last month and said Russian reforms were still on track.
Economists said budget revenues were likely to remain a key concern to the IMF for the rest of this year and beyond.
"There has been a lot of attention on the part of the government and it is beginning to show some results. Things are moving in the right direction," one Western economist said.
The IMF last month set a new target for the 1996 budget deficit of 5.25 percent of gross domestic product. The previous target was four percent.

An early draft of the 1997 budget foresees a deficit of 3.3 percent, using Russian methods of calculating the gap. But economists and State Duma deputies have been sceptical about whether revenues will be enough to meet this.
The budget deficit widened in the summer partly as a result of paying sky-high yields on Treasury bills to investors nervous ahead of the presidential election.
International monetary sources in Washington say the IMF wants Russia to make its government securities market more open to foreigners, partly to bring down interest rates.
Russia eased non-residents' access to the market last month but yields are capped and other restrictions remain.
